evaluations.title: Is ICL Sophisticated Pattern-Matching?
evaluations.reasoning: Active research at major conferences (ICLR 2024, ICML 2024, NeurIPS 2024). ICL is now understood as under-specified program induction and algorithm selection, not simple pattern matching. Multiple papers demonstrate sophisticated algorithm re-weighting based on in-context examples.

evaluations.title: Is ICL Due to Mesa-Optimization?
evaluations.reasoning: The 2023 paper 'Uncovering mesa-optimization algorithms in Transformers' (updated Oct 2024) demonstrates that standard next-token prediction gives rise to a subsidiary learning algorithm that adjusts the model as new inputs are revealed. This corresponds to gradient-based optimization of a principled objective function. While ongoing work continues on architectural implications, the core question has been answered affirmatively.

evidence.title: Uncovering mesa-optimization algorithms in Transformers
evidence.key_finding: Next-token prediction error minimization gives rise to subsidiary learning algorithm (mesa-optimizer) that adjusts model as new inputs revealed

evidence.title: On Mesa-Optimization in Autoregressively Trained Transformers: Emergence and Capability

title: Does Scaling Improve Reasoning Capabilities?
reasoning: Major breakthroughs in 2024 with o1/o3 models demonstrating BOTH train-time and test-time compute scaling improve reasoning. New dimension discovered: test-time compute (TTC) scaling via chain-of-thought. RL-trained reasoning shows consistent improvements with more thinking time. Definitively addressed with clear empirical evidence.

evidence.title: OpenAI o1: Learning to Reason with LLMs

title: How Does Finetuning Change a Pretrained Model?
reasoning: ICLR 2024 research demonstrates finetuning ENHANCES existing mechanisms rather than fundamentally altering them. Same computational circuits used, but with improved sub-mechanisms. Also shown to internalize biases from training data. Mechanistic interpretability revealing specific layer effects.

evidence.title: Fine-Tuning Enhances Existing Mechanisms: A Case Study on Entity Tracking

title: Can Interpretability Methods Maintain Validity When Used to Modify Model Behavior?
reasoning: Strong theoretical foundations emerging in 2024-2025. Causal abstraction framework provides theoretical foundation for intervention validity. Methods like activation patching and causal tracing designed explicitly for causal interventions. Active research with formal causal frameworks.

evidence.title: The Quest for the Right Mediator: Mechanistic Interpretability Through Causal Mediation Analysis
Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability

title: Standardized Evaluations of Jailbreak and Prompt Injection Success
reasoning: Multiple standardized benchmarks emerged in 2024. JailbreakBench (NeurIPS 2024) provides comprehensive framework with 100 behaviors. GenTel-Bench offers 84k prompt injection examples. Multiple other benchmarks from late 2024. Leaderboards tracking attack/defense performance.

title: Justifying Value Choices for Alignment
reasoning: Extensive philosophical work on 'whose values?' problem with multiple frameworks proposed (democratic AI ethics, Rawlsian reasonable pluralism). Active 2024 research. However, this is fundamentally a normative question that may not have a single 'solution' - ongoing philosophical debate with multiple valid perspectives.

evidence.title: Democratizing value alignment: from authoritarian to democratic AI ethics

title: Misinformation and Manipulation
reasoning: Extensive research on dual nature of LLMs: they both generate misinformation at scale AND help detect it. AI-generated content often more credible than human-written. Detection models struggling (performance degradation). 2024 datasets and detection methods emerging. Active arms race, not solved.

evidence.title: Combating misinformation in the age of LLMs: Opportunities and challenges

title: Overreliance
reasoning: Systematic reviews examining 35+ studies. Well-documented automation bias problem. LLMs exacerbate issue (fluency, persuasiveness). Mitigation attempts (explanations) largely ineffective. Active research but no good solutions yet.

evidence.title: Exploring automation bias in human–AI collaboration: a review and implications for explainable AI

title: Global Economic Development
reasoning: IMF/UN/World Bank 2024-2025 reports provide extensive analysis. Clear finding: AI likely to worsen global inequality. 40% of jobs affected globally; developing countries lack infrastructure to benefit. $4.8T market by 2033, concentrated in advanced economies. 118 countries absent from governance. Policy recommendations exist, implementation is the challenge.

evidence.title: AI Will Transform the Global Economy
